title: Regional Spend Thermostat: soft+hard spend caps with device-aware fallback
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: We need a router-level 'Regional Spend Thermostat' to control cross-region and cross-tier spending on inference requests for multi-tenant workloads. The thermostat enforces soft and hard caps per region and per budget group while selecting GPU families and model variants (e.g., quantized or smaller variant) as graceful degradation. It should prioritize SLO-critical tenants and provide telemetry for chargebacks.
problem_statement: Current routing routes by simple priority and availability. During spot shortages or regional price spikes, costs balloon and tenants can unexpectedly consume expensive on-demand GPUs across regions. We lack an automated, tenant-aware mechanism to throttle or downgrade requests when spend thresholds are approaching, and to select cheaper device classes or model variants proactively.
goals: Prevent >X% unexpected month-over-month spend increases from cross-region fallback to on-demand GPUs
Provide configurable soft caps (throttle/queue) and hard caps (reject) per region/tier/budget-group
Automatically fallback to lower-cost model variants or quantized runtimes before escalating to on-demand instances
Expose per-tenant and per-route telemetry for costs, evictions, and fallback events
Prioritize SLO-critical requests and honor tenant reserved capacity (Dedicated)
non_goals: Microbilling UI in Console (separate PM ticket)
Changes to core kernel selection heuristics unrelated to routing decisions
Implementing a new pricing engine — we will use existing cost estimates and spot price feed
design_notes: Thermostat concept: maintain a sliding-window spend budget for (region, tier, budget_group). Two thresholds: soft_threshold (e.g., 80% of allocated budget) triggers progressive degradation policies: (1) prefer cheaper GPU families (e.g., a100 -> a10x), (2) route to quantized model variant, (3) enable batching or increased preemption window. Hard_threshold (e.g., 100%) results in user-configurable actions: reject, rate-limit, or route to a paid-on-demand fallback only for high-priority tenants. Use tokenized cost model and per-request cost estimate calculated from model variant, sequence length quantile, and device-type unit price. Maintain safety headroom and predictive short-term forecasting to avoid oscillation.
tradeoffs: Complexity vs predictability: predictive throttling reduces surprises but increases router state and compute overhead
Fairness vs SLO: prioritizing high-SLA tenants can starve free/low-tier users in a region during spot scarcity
Cost accuracy vs latency: more accurate per-request cost estimates require additional profiling data; fallback decisions must be fast
Operational burden: more control knobs (soft/hard caps, degradation order) increase configuration surface for support
policy_spec_summary: Policy object identifies scope (region(s), tier(s), budget_group, tenant_selector). Fields: soft_cap_usd_per_hour, hard_cap_usd_per_hour, soft_action_sequence (ordered list of actions), hard_action (reject|limit|fallback-on-demand-with-chargeback), hedging_ratio (reserve extra headroom for spot eviction probability), priority_override_list. Router evaluates current spend window and projected spend; if projected > soft_cap -> apply first matching soft_action; if projected > hard_cap -> apply hard_action.
acceptance_criteria: Router can evaluate spend per (region, tier, budget_group) on a 1-min sliding window
Soft cap trigger leads to at least one degradation action (gpu-family or model-variant) within 5s for newly arriving requests
Hard cap enforcement returns configured response (429 or rejection) and logs event to audit log
Telemetry shows correct attribution of cost to tenant and region in trace and Console dashboard
E2E test simulating spot eviction results in thermostat shifting >70% of overflow to quantized variants rather than on-demand luxuries
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Lightweight prototype in router that reads static policy and enforces prefer_gpu_families + model_variant_ranking (2w)
Phase 2: Sliding-window spend accounting service (prometheus-compatible metrics + small Redis estimation layer) (3w)
Phase 3: Hedging and predictive projection using last-N minutes burn-rate + spot-price feed integration (2w)
Phase 4: Console UI for policy authoring + audit logs (PM/Design parallel work) (3w)
Phase 5: Gradual rollout (canary per region -> 25% tenants -> global) and observability tuning (2w)
risky_areas_and_mitigation: Incorrect cost estimates -> mitigation: conservative multiplier and safety headroom
Oscillation between regions after quick price change -> mitigation: cooldown window and rate-limited decision changes
Tenant surprise on silent degradation -> mitigation: user-visible warnings, opt-in beta, and billing alerts
Performance impact on router decision latency -> mitigation: cache decisions for short TTL and use async accounting updates
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation engine
Load tests simulating regional surge with spot evictions and validating degradation order
Chaos test where region A is fully evicted: ensure router does not flood region B and honors thermostat caps
Integration test validating billing attribution and Console dashboard correctness
Contract tests for interaction between router and serving runtime about model_variant compatibility
rollout_plan: Start with non-critical low-traffic region as canary for 48h. Monitor metrics_to_track; if soft_threshold_triggers_count > baseline but latency within SLO and cost reduces, expand to 25% of tenants (traffic-based). For any hard_cap enforcement, alert on-call and auto-disable policy if hard enforcement rate exceeds threshold for >15m.
observability_and_alerting: Create Dashboards: Thermostat overview (per-region spend, headroom), Degradation heatmap (which actions fired), Latency and error breakdowns. Alerts: spend_projection_exceeds_hard_cap (P0), repeated_soft_action_burst (P1). Integrate with PagerDuty runbook.
migration_and_backward_compatibility: Default policies are disabled. There will be a feature flag per region. Existing routes without budget_group field default to global shared budget with conservative soft caps. Ensure dedicated capacity tenants have override to always bypass thermostat if they hold reserved capacity.
security_and_compliance: All policy changes are auditable and stored in encrypted config store. Audit logs capture who changed caps. No customer data is sent to third parties; spot-price feed is from an internal vendor API with limited scope.
owner_notes: We should keep the initial policy surface small: region and budget_group only. If this proves stable, extend to per-route revenue-aware caps. Coordinate with Pricing and Account teams for sensible defaults and tenant notifications.
